findings.title: mobileOverview returns an unbounded nested payload with no pagination contract
findings.why_it_matters: The new mobileOverview query is the single backend contract powering the dashboard, yet it loads up to 1,000 deals, 500 activities, 2,000 posted invoices, and 2,000 month invoices in one response. For any medium workspace this response will hit Convex function limits and there is no cursor, page size, or pagination metadata for clients to degrade gracefully.
evidence: Return object includes full overdueInvoices array and recentActivities array with no limit contract other than a hardcoded .slice(0,5)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the monolithic query with targeted aggregate queries (count, sum) for KPIs and a separate paginated query for recent/overdue lists. Return a contract that includes pageInfo or at least explicit limit fields so mobile can handle large orgs.

findings.title: Invoice detail casts user-supplied id through a type assertion instead of a validated contract
findings.why_it_matters: Deep-link and route parameters arrive as strings. Casting `id as Id<'invoices'>` bypasses Convex's generated type safety and any input validation. A malformed or cross-table id is passed straight to api.invoices.getById, relying entirely on backend authorization that is not visible in this diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the id shape before passing it to the query, or use a typed route param parser. Avoid the `as Id<...>` cast; rely on Convex's generated validators by passing the raw string through a client-side check and letting the backend validator reject invalid ids.

findings.title: Auth token exchange contract lacks timeout and error-shape guarantees
findings.why_it_matters: exchangeConvexToken normalizes the Better Auth convex.token() response to string|null, but the contract says nothing about how long the call may take, what happens when the server is unreachable, or whether errors are logged. Convex will call this fetcher repeatedly for token refresh; a hanging call leaves the connection in an indeterminate authenticated state.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/lib/auth-client.ts:58 exchangeConvexToken awaits authClient.convex.token() with no timeout
The function returns null on both 'no session' and 'error' cases, collapsing two distinct outcomes into one contract value
findings.suggested_fix: Add a documented timeout (e.g., 10-15s) with AbortSignal, distinguish transient errors from missing-session null returns, and ensure the losing promise is caught to avoid unhandled rejections.

findings.title: Shared env schema forces mobile to stub a server-only secret
findings.why_it_matters: The platform-agnostic Env type requires BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, which is meaningless on a mobile client. Mobile satisfies the contract by stubbing a placeholder, but this creates a dangerous invariant: the shared schema cannot safely add more server-only secrets without every client having to fake them. A future refactor could accidentally wire the stub into the public bundle.
evidence: packages/config/src/env.ts:42 BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: z.string().min(1) is required in the shared schema
findings.suggested_fix: Split the schema into clientEnvSchema (CONVEX_URL, CONVEX_SITE_URL, SITE_URL, NODE_ENV) and serverEnvSchema (client + BETTER_AUTH_SECRET + OAuth secrets). Mobile imports and validates only the client schema.

findings.title: New mobile Convex queries have no versioning or deprecation strategy
findings.why_it_matters: mobileOverview and agingDeals are new public query contracts consumed by a mobile client that may lag behind the backend. Once shipped, changing response shapes or removing fields will break installed app binaries that cannot be updated instantly. There is no naming convention, version field, or deprecation path.
evidence: No version suffix, compatibility layer, or changelog is present
findings.suggested_fix: Document the mobile query contracts and adopt additive-only changes for the MVP. For future iterations, introduce either versioned exports (e.g. mobileOverviewV2) or a mobile API version header/argument before making breaking changes.

residual_risks: The mobile app imports api and Id from a deep relative path re-export (../../../../convex/_generated). A change in the generated output location would break mobile builds silently at type-check time.
No schema is enforced for the deep-link route params beyond TypeScript; malformed ids from push notifications or universal links may crash before reaching the backend.
testing_gaps: Contract test asserting mobileOverview response shape against a Zod/JSON schema so mobile client types stay in sync.
Integration test that exercises exchangeConvexToken timeout and null/error contract paths.
